 Live Updates Updated Thu, Nov 19 2026 1:24 PM EST Share Share Article via Facebook Share Article via Twitter Share Article via LinkedIn Share Article via Email Anthropic IPO live updates: AI lab tops $2 trillion market cap, Ashton Kutcher celebrates debut
 Ashley Capoot Caleigh Keating Samantha Subin Greg Iacurci This is CNBC live coverage of Anthropic's IPO and Nasdaq debut. 
 watch now VIDEO 1:10 01:10 Anthropic opens at $111.50 per share in record IPO Squawk on the Street Anthropic opened at $111.50 per share in the artificial intelligence lab's Nasdaq debut on Thursday after the company completed the biggest initial public offering on record.
 The stock will trade under the ticker "ANT" after the company raised $81.3 billion in the IPO. The Claude creator sold 980 million shares at $83 a piece on Wednesday, lifting the size and price of its offering.
 The 5-year-old company captivated the corporate world with its Claude AI models and products, which have fueled its meteoric rise this year. Anthropic said in its prospectus that it generated $33.24 billion in revenue for the nine months ended Sept. 30, up a staggering 1,200% from the same period last year.
 Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei co-founded the company in 2021 after he and a small group of researchers defected from OpenAI , now its chief rival. Anthropic has faced sharp criticism over its positions on safety, regulation and national security, including by President Donald Trump and other senior government officials. 
 Highlights so far:
 Ashton Kutcher congratulates the AI lab
 Market cap tops $2 trillion in debut, putting it among the tech titans
 ANT stock pops in first trade 
 Protesters gather outside the Nasdaq
 Daniela Amodei gives a shoutout to mom 
 Dario Amodei addresses debt and landing an investment-grade credit rating
 Spotted: Executives sporting "Clawd" pins at Nasdaq
 Dario Amodei renews pledge to pace frontier AI development 
 Retail demand for ANT was the largest in history
 Anthropic employees set to get rich 
 CNBC's reporters are covering Anthropic's IPO live on air and online from our bureaus in San Francisco and Englewood Cliffs, New Jersey, and from the Nasdaq in New York City. 
 VIDEO 15:11 15:11 Watch CNBC’s full interview with Anthropic co-founders Dario and Daniela Amodei 11 Min Ago Can Anthropic make cyber its next big market? Wolfe Research sees coding-sized opportunity
 Samuel Boivin | Nurphoto | Getty Images Anthropic has made headlines in recent months for its advanced artificial intelligence models with sophisticated cybersecurity capabilities.
 The company limited access to its widely known Mythos model to select customers through Project Glasswing this year in a bid to curb the risk of bad actors using and exploiting it. 
 Anthropic has since broadened the pool of testers and launched cybersecurity initiative aimed at protecting critical infrastructure. 
 These moves have raised questions over whether the company will scale its cybersecurity business — or even pit it against major security vendors, including partners.
 That opportunity could match Anthropic's coding opportunity and reach $500 billion annually, Wolfe Research analysts wrote in a Thursday note.
 "Act 2 is Cyber which given the last week seems like it could be as big as Coding," they wrote. 
 That market might include AI security operations, patching or penetration testing — simulated cyberattacks utilized to identity a company's security weaknesses. 
 "We think that model providers will offer a solution to replace the security team that is manually analyzing data with agents who can respond at machine speed," they added. 
 — Samantha Subin 
 41 Min Ago Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley rake in fees from Anthropic IPO
 Anthropic PBC signage at the Morgan Stanley headquarters during the Anthropic PBC initial public offering (IPO) in New York, US, on Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026. Adam Gray | Bloomberg | Getty Images Wall Street banks are set to reap a huge windfall from Anthropic's IPO, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley among the biggest earners. 
 The company disclosed in its latest SEC filing that it agreed to pay the banks $550 million, surpassing the roughly $500 million payday banks took in from SpaceX's IPO in June.
 — Annie Palmer 
 48 Min Ago Anthropic's partners take a victory lap
 Anthropic's investors and other partners are taking a victory lap upon the AI lab's successful debut. 
 Investors Menlo Ventures and Lightspeed dedicated the front page of their websites to congratulating Anthropic, as did counsel Wilson Sonsini Goodrich & Rosati . Bessemer's Byron Deeter posted a thread on X detailing the backstory of the firm's investment in Anthropic. 
 — Caleigh Keating 
 56 Min Ago Menlo Ventures has $25 billion aggregate position in Anthropic, partner Matt Murphy says
 Close-up of sign for Menlo Ventures, San Francisco, California, March 12, 2026. Smith Collection | Gado | Archive Photos | Getty Images Menlo Ventures partner Matt Murphy, an early Anthropic investor, said the firm's aggregate position in the AI company is around $25 billion.
 "Clearly the most epic return for Menlo Ventures in our history, and one of the top handful in the history of venture capital," Murphy told CNBC in an interview. "We feel grateful. We have over five LPs that we've delivered over a billion dollars of returns to, and at the end of the day, that's really our job."
 — Ashley Capoot 
 1 Hour Ago Ashton Kutcher celebrates Anthropic IPO
 Michael Kovac Ashton Kutcher congratulated Dario Amodei and "the whole team at Anthropic" in a post on X shortly before the AI company's first trade.
 Kutcher co-founded Sound Ventures , a Los Angeles-based venture capital firm, which invested in Anthropic in 2023 and participated in several subsequent funding rounds. The VC firm also counts Guy Oseary, the legendary talent manager for musicians including Madonna, among its cofounders. 
 Bloomberg reported that Sound Ventures owns roughly half a percent of Anthropic, citing sources familiar with the matter. 
 Sound Ventures' stake is likely now worth billions of dollars after the company's lofty IPO. 
 — Annie Palmer 
 1 Hour Ago Bessemer's Deeter calls Anthropic IPO a "Google moment"
 Byron Deeter, a partner at Bessemer Venture Partners, called Anthropic 's IPO a " Google moment" for the frontier lab during CNBC's Halftime Report.
 At over $2 trillion in market capitalization, Anthropic has entered Google's ranks as one of the most valuable companies in the world, behind Apple , Microsoft , Nvidia , Alphabet (Google's parent company), and Amazon . 
 But Deeter says Anthropic doesn't need to "dominate intelligence" in the same way that Google dominates search.
 The artificial intelligence ecosystem will see "multiple great businesses," Deeter says, adding that he expects Anthropic to continue to be a market leader while also pacing the frontier of AI model development.
 — Isabel O'Brien 
 1 Hour Ago Anthropic’s governance structure
 Anthropic Co-Founder and CEO Dario Amodei speaks at Dreamforce 2026 summit in San Francisco, California, U.S., September 15, 2026. Carlos Barria | Reuters Anthropic has an unusual governance structure .
 The company is a public benefit corporation, which means it's required to balance the financial interest of stockholders, the best interests of those affected by its conduct and its "company purpose." Anthropic said in its prospectus that its purpose is to facilitate the "responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity."
 Anthropic's seven co-founders also wield a lot of power over the company. Prior to the completion of its offering, Anthropic issued a single share of Class F common stock to a limited liability company called "Founder LLC." Anthropic's co-founders are the sole members of Founder LLC, and the entity holds 50.1% of the voting power of the company's outstanding shares.
 Each co-founder sold 3.38 million shares in the IPO, according to the prospectus, for total proceeds of $1.96 billion.
 Additionally, Anthropic introduced an independent governance body called the " Long-Term Benefit Trust " in 2023, which has the authority to elect and remove the majority of the company's board of directors. 
 — Ashley Capoot 
 1 Hour Ago Anthropic's market cap tops $2 trillion in Nasdaq debut
 Anthropic opened with a market capitalization of nearly $2.01 trillion, behind only Apple , Microsoft , Nvidia , Alphabet and Amazon .
 — Ashley Capoot 
 2 Hours Ago Ben Bernanke is in the room
 Ben Bernanke T.J. Kirkpatrick | Bloomberg | Getty Images Ben Bernanke, the former chair of the Federal Reserve , is in the room at the Nasdaq as investors celebrate Anthropic's first trade. 
 Anthropic in July appointed Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust, the AI company's independent governance structure that advises it and appoints its board members. 
 — Annie Palmer 
 2 Hours Ago Anthropic shares pop 34% in Nasdaq debut
 Anthropic shares popped 34% in the company's Nasdaq debut.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Anthropic stock price. — Ashley Capoot 
 2 Hours Ago Anthropic is indicated to open at $111 per share, source says
 Anthropic is indicated to open at $111 per share, a person familiar told CNBC.
 — Ashley Capoot 
 2 Hours Ago Anthropic is indicated to open at $110 a share, source says
 Anthropic is indicated to open at $110 a share, a person familiar told CNBC.
 — Ashley Capoot 
 2 Hours Ago Amodei touts Anthropic’s focus on culture and talent
 Dario Amodei, co-founder and chief executive officer of Anthropic, during the company's Builder Summit in Bengaluru, India, on Monday, Feb. 16, 2026. Samyukta Lakshmi | Bloomberg | Getty Images Amodei told JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon in a fireside chat on Friday that he thinks talent and culture are the "most important things" that drive a company's success, which is why he and his co-founders have tried to place so much emphasis on those areas at Anthropic. 
 Anthropic requires every employee to pass a culture interview, which is taken very seriously, Amodei said. He added that he spends roughly half of his time focusing on talent and culture at the company. 
 "We've been very disciplined about turning down people who are deeply technically talented, but who don't fit our culture," Amodei said. "We don't want people who are jerks. We don't want people who try to steal the show and don't work well with others. We don't want people who aren't oriented towards the public benefit."
 Amodei also regularly holds DVQs, which stands for "Dario Vision Quests," where he speaks in front of the entire company. He said he tries to update employees by talking honestly and avoiding "corpo speak."
 "It means that the leaders of the company can trust the employees," Amodei said. "The employees of the company can trust the leaders of the company to be candid. Everyone feels that we're being honest with them, and that has this enormous value."
 — Ashley Capoot 
 2 Hours Ago Ben Reitzes: 'The leverage here could be insane'
 watch now VIDEO 4:23 04:23 Melius initiates coverage of Anthropic with buy rating and price target of $155 Squawk on the Street Ben Reitzes, head of technology research at Melius, said growth and leverage as well as efficiency gains outweigh margin concerns when it comes to estimating Anthropic's future growth path.
 "They're ahead of the game in models, making them more efficient, and their cost to train is going down, and the speed to train is going down. So they're going to be putting out models at such a rapid clip that are on the frontier," Reitzes told CNBC's "Squawk on the Street." 
 "That makes them more valuable and worth paying for."
 Melius initiated coverage of Anthropic with a buy rating and price target of $155 per share. Reitzes said Melius compared Anthropic to hyperscalers and said its assigned value could even be "conservative."
 "The reason it's conservative is much better growth, and the leverage here could be insane."
 — Caleigh Keating 
 2 Hours Ago Half of institutional investors who put in orders were left empty-handed, sources say
 Anthropic billboards are displayed in Times Square as shares begin trading after their IPO on November 19, 2026 in New York City. Michael M. Santiago | Getty Images Anthropic prioritized allocating shares to institutional investors it had relationships with, according to people familiar with the details, who asked not to be named because they were not authorized to speak publicly. That meant roughly half of the firms that placed orders were left empty-handed, they said.
 It's normal in most IPOs for some portion of institutional investors not to receive any allocation, but that was a higher number than usual for this offering, one person said. Anthropic's management team had experience working with institutional investors from raising capital through private rounds, so the company had a strong view of what would make up a good shareholder base construction, the person said.
 Retail allocation came in at around 15%, the people said. Anthropic had estimated that about 20% of the offering would go to retail, as CNBC previously reported, a higher percentage than the typical 5% to 10% allotment.
 — Leslie Picker and Ashley Capoot 
 2 Hours Ago Protestors gather outside the Nasdaq
 Demonstrators hold a banner during the Anthropic PBC initial public offering (IPO) at the Nasdaq MarketSite in New York, US, on Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026. Adam Gray | Bloomberg | Getty Images Protestors are gathering outside of the Nasdaq ahead of the listing. 
 The New York City Democratic Socialists of America shared a post on Instagram on Wednesday encouraging demonstrators to attend a rally at 9 a.m. ET on Thursday. The group said Anthropic "is driving the AI bubble to get rich quick before the bubble bursts."
 Demonstrators against artificial intelligence (AI) hold banners during the Anthropic PBC initial public offering (IPO) at the Nasdaq MarketSite in New York, US, on Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026. Adam Gray | Bloomberg | Getty Images "Join our rally to send a message to all Big Tech oligarchs and demand a freeze to reckless AI development and destruction," the group said.
 Other organizations, including Climate Defiance, Act Up and New York Communities for Change are also sponsoring the protest.
 NYPD officers arrest protesters for blocking the doors to the Nasdaq MarketSite as shares of Anthropic begin trading after their IPO on November 19, 2026 in Times Square, New York City. Michael M. Santiago | Getty Images — Ashley Capoot 
 2 Hours Ago Goldman and Morgan Stanley led the IPO
 Anthropic PBC signage at the Morgan Stanley headquarters in New York, US, on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Images As with SpaceX's offering, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley led Anthropic's IPO. Some 20 other banks are listed on the prospectus, including JPMorgan Chase , Citigroup and Barclays . 
 — Ari Levy 
 3 Hours Ago Investors who flip IPO may face penalty
 Retail investors with access to the Anthropic IPO who try to sell the stock for a quick profit may face a penalty from their brokerage . 
 Anthropic made shares available to retail investors through brokerages including Charles Schwab, Fidelity, Robinhood, SoFi, E-Trade and some of their respective affiliates, the AI startup said in an IPO prospectus. 
 Many of them have "anti-flipping" policies meant to discourage investors who purchase IPO shares from dumping them fast.
 These policies apply only to retail investors who place an order with their brokerage firm to buy the Anthropic IPO at its offering price — something many investors don't have access to.
 For example, Fidelity clients who sell IPO shares within the first 15 calendar days from the start of trading in the secondary market would be barred from participating in future stock IPOs through the brokerage. Investors get a six-month ban after the first offense and could be permanently barred after the third offense.
 — Greg Iacurci 
 3 Hours Ago Anthropic shares indicated to open at $105, source says open expected in next hour
 Anthropic is indicated to open at $105 a share, representing a nearly 27% jump from its $83 IPO price. 
 A source familiar with the matter told CNBC that the stock is expected to open this hour. 
 — Samantha Subin 
 3 Hours Ago Anthropic’s strained relationship with the Trump administration
 Dario Amodei, co-founded Anthropic, takes questions alongside Mark Zuckerberg, CEO of Meta Platforms, and U.S. President Donald Trump as Trump holds a press briefing with AI executives following a meeting on artificial intelligence outside the West Wing of the White House on September 29, 2026 in Washington, DC. Kevin Dietsch | Getty Images Anthropic has had two major disputes with the Trump administration this year, but tensions have begun to thaw between the two camps in recent months. 
 Amodei joined Trump for a private dinner at the White House in September, which marked the first one-on-one meeting between the two leaders. Days later, Amodei attended a luncheon at the White House, where he signed a voluntary AI safety accord.
 Three months earlier, the company had to temporarily disable access to two of its most advanced models, Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5, in order to comply with an export control directive from the government that cited "national security authorities." Anthropic restored the models after roughly two weeks of tense negotiations.
 In March, Anthropic was banned by the Pentagon after discussions about how the military could use its AI models spiraled out of control. The company sued the Trump administration to try to reverse the blacklisting. 
 — Ashley Capoot 
 3 Hours Ago How to get Anthropic stock — without buying the IPO
 Retail investors who don't want to buy Anthropic stock directly will get access to the AI startup courtesy of many popular mutual funds and exchange-traded funds . 
 Index funds won't add Anthropic stock immediately. Some will add them within days or weeks, depending on the inclusion rules of specific indexes.
 For example, the Morningstar U.S. Total Market Index will add the stock after five trading days. The Nasdaq-100 will add it after Dec. 18. The S&P 500 won't add it for at least a year. 
 Many actively managed funds held pre-IPO Anthropic shares — and investors in those funds automatically get a sliver of Anthropic's IPO when it starts trading. A handful of the most heavily concentrated funds held pre-IPO shares worth more than 10% of their overall portfolios. 
 Most investors' exposure to Anthropic in mutual funds and ETFs will likely be relatively low — well below 1% of the overall portfolio for most funds, experts said. 
 — Greg Iacurci 
 3 Hours Ago Daniela Amodei gives shoutout to mom
 watch now VIDEO 0:54 00:54 Anthropic’s sibling founders reflect on IPO journey: 'I hope you are watching. If you are, hi, Mom!' Squawk on the Street Daniela Amodei said she and Dario are "so proud" of the Anthropic team. 
 "Dario and I were talking about this beforehand: This is such an incredible milestone," she said. "It's such a huge moment for the company. We're so proud of what the team has done to get us here, and also, we're the same company." 
 "We're so excited to continue pursuing our mission. I think that's the thing we're both really focused on, and also we're hoping to be able to spend a little more time together, just the two of us as siblings, after this is over," she added.
 Daniela also shouted out the siblings' mom.
 "I hope you're watching. If you are, hi, Mom!," she said.
 — Ashley Capoot 
 3 Hours Ago No updates on clash with Pentagon
 Daniela Amodei said there were no significant updates on Anthropic's clash with the Department of Defense but expects the company's relationship with the government to continue.
 "My feeling, honestly, at Anthropic is that we have always worked extremely well with the national security apparatus of the United States of America. We're very committed to ensuring that Claude is helping to protect the nation. We've had an incredible working relationship with that entire part of the government, really since Anthropic was founded, and we expect that that will continue."
 — Caleigh Keating 
 3 Hours Ago Dario Amodei says $900 billion commitments don't 'seem so large'
 watch now VIDEO 1:12 01:12 Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei says $900 billion commitments don’t ‘seem so large’ Squawk on the Street Dario Amodei defended the company's massive $900 billion in AI commitments.
 "If you look at the amount of cash we have on the balance sheet and the amount of revenue that we're already making per year, suddenly those commitments don't seem so large," he said.
 Amodei said the company tries to "err on the low side" when predicting compute.
 — Samantha Subin 
 3 Hours Ago Dario Amodei: Anthropic 'enjoying' working with SpaceX
 watch now VIDEO 1:00 01:00 Anthropic is ‘enjoying’ working with SpaceX, says CEO Dario Amodei Squawk on the Street Dario Amodei said Anthropic is "enjoying" working with SpaceX amid speculation the company might scale back use of SpaceX's compute.
 "You can't be sure what you're going to do in the future. But you know, we're finding that compute to be high quality. We're enjoying working with SpaceX."
 — Caleigh Keating 
 3 Hours Ago Amodeis decline to comment on whether Jensen Huang should return as Nvidia CEO
 watch now VIDEO 3:20 03:20 Amodeis decline to comment on whether Huang should return as Nvidia CEO: ‘That’s up to Nvidia’ Squawk on the Street Dario Amodei said Anthropic has had "a long and productive partnership" with Nvidia, but he and Daniela declined to comment on whether Jensen Huang should return as the company's CEO.
 — Ashley Capoot 
 3 Hours Ago Dario Amodei: Anthropic hopes to secure investment-grade credit rating in future
 watch now VIDEO 3:33 03:33 Anthropic hopes to secure investment-grade credit rating in future, says CEO Dario Amodei Squawk on the Street Dario Amodei said Anthropic is "hoping" to secure an investment-grade credit rating in the future.
 "Obviously we will see how that turns out," he said.
 "Debt is an instrument that we have available to us, and we'd like to use at some point in the future," he added.
 — Ashley Capoot 
 3 Hours Ago Daniela Amodei: Anthropic is a 'safety-first' company
 watch now VIDEO 1:39 01:39 Daniela Amodei: Anthropic is a ‘safety-first’ company Squawk on the Street Daniela Amodei said Anthropic bears responsibility to ensure alignment within models and engage with consumers in order to mitigate risk.
 "Anthropic has been a safety company, a safety-first company, from day one," Amodei said.
 "The promise is incredible, and the risks are real. And we were really founded on this idea that it is our job to mitigate those risks, and I think we have to date done an incredible job doing that. We obviously have more work ahead of us, but we are deeply committed to safety."
 — Caleigh Keating 
 3 Hours Ago Dario Amodei on pressure: 'We've been calm about it'
 watch now VIDEO 1:09 01:09 Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on handling pressure: ‘We’ve been calm about it’ Squawk on the Street The pressure is on Anthropic over the expectations tied to being the largest IPO on record. 
 "We've been calm about it," CEO Dario Amodei said.
 Despite the turn in the spotlight, Amodei said the company is laser-focused on the fundamentals.
 "We always want to under promise and over deliver," he said. "You know, that's our core."
 — Samantha Subin 
 3 Hours Ago Daniela Amodei: Will listen to communities on data centers
 Daniela Amodei, President, co-founder, and Chair of the Board of Directors at Anthropic, speaking to CNBC on Nov. 19th, 2026. CNBC Daniela Amodei said the company is focusing on listening to consumers when it comes to data centers in the wake of the midterms.
 "One of the things that I think is really important to Anthropic is for it to feel to people like this technology is not happening to them. And I think really from our perspective, building data centers is something where we also need to listen to what it is that those communities want and help to bring forward that future as well."
 — Caleigh Keating 
 3 Hours Ago Daniela Amodei: Anthropic's debut is 'one stop on the journey'
 watch now VIDEO 3:30 03:30 Anthropic’s debut is ‘one stop on the journey,' says Daniela Amodei Squawk on the Street Daniela Amodei said Anthropic is a "long-term focused company," so it thinks about its debut as just one step along its journey.
 "While today is a super exciting milestone, and we're obviously really, really excited about it, I think it's, for us, it's like one stop on the journey," she said. "We think about this as, 'Wow, this is an incredible moment for Anthropic for our mission, but we're going to wake up tomorrow and we're going to be the same company.'"
 — Ashley Capoot 
 3 Hours Ago Daniela Amodei talks public benefit structure
 Anthropic President Daniela Amodei touted the company's public benefit structure.
 "We're really trying to do something that we do think can have this incredible economic value and impact, but we want it to be baked into essentially our structure," she said.
 — Samantha Subin 
 3 Hours Ago Dario Amodei: Balancing between growth and pacing a 'central tension'
 Dario Amodei said the balance between growth and pacing was one of the "central tensions" at the heart of Anthropic.
 "What we've done with pacing is essentially said, look, we could drive at 200 miles an hour. Maybe let's only drive at 90 miles an hour. Spend time figuring out how to do that safely, and the rest of that surplus we spend building the model in the right way."
 — Caleigh Keating 
 3 Hours Ago Amodei on scaling laws: 'I don't think we really believed it until it actually happened'
 watch now VIDEO 3:52 03:52 Anthropic CEO on scaling laws: ‘I don’t think we really believed it until it actually happened’ Squawk on the Street Dario Amodei said while the scaling laws behind AI suggested the technology would become extremely capable, even he has been surprised to see it play out.
 "The scaling laws kind of imply that the technology and hopefully our work within it would have this scale, but I don't think we really believed it until it actually happened," he said. "And it's happening right now."
 — Ashley Capoot 
 3 Hours Ago Anthropic underwriters have the option to purchase up to an additional 147 million shares
 Anthropic said its underwriters have the option to purchase up to an additional 147 million shares of Class A common stock from the company, according to a Thursday filing , which would net the company another $12.2 billion. 
 Assuming that option is exercised, Anthropic would raise a total of $93.5 billion through its IPO, topping the $85.7 billion raised by SpaceX.
 Anthropic's underwriters have until Nov. 20 to exercise the option.
 — Ashley Capoot 
 4 Hours Ago Anthropic executives wear "Clawd" pins to ring opening bell
 A pin worn by CEO of Anthropic Dario Amodei inside the Nasdaq MarketSite ahead of the anticipated IPO of artificial intelligence company Anthropic in New York City on November 19, 2026. Charly Triballeau | Afp | Getty Images Anthropic executives were sporting "Clawd" pins while they rang the opening bell at the Nasdaq.
 Clawd is a pixelated crab mascot that the company associates with Claude Code, its popular AI coding product. 
 — Ashley Capoot 
 4 Hours Ago Brad Gerstner: Anthropic not a 'get-rich-quick scheme'
 watch now VIDEO 8:16 08:16 Brad Gerstner on $5B Anthropic investment: A cornerstone investment for Altimeter Squawk Box Brad Gerstner, founder and CEO of Altimeter Captial, said Anthropic's ability to disprove profitability concerns and make their market debut despite recent headwinds and market pressures facing the tech industry demonstrated how "extraordinary" the company is.
 "I think this level of demand for the company from Altimeter and others, and from retail investors getting in the game, getting their shot on goal the first time, is real evidence of just how extraordinary this company has operated," Gerstner told CNBC's "Squawk Box."
 Gerstner's Altimeter Capital is planning on investing $5 billion in the AI lab, which he called a "cornerstone" investment for his firm.
 "This isn't a get-rich-quick scheme. As I've said, this will be a cornerstone investment for Altimeter. This is a multi-year compounder in the most important super cycle in the history of technology," Gerstner told CNBC.
 — Caleigh Keating 
 4 Hours Ago Amodei renews pledge to pace the development of AI in Nasdaq speech
 watch now VIDEO 5:14 05:14 Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei renews pledge to pace the development of AI in Nasdaq speech Squawk on the Street Amodei is speaking about AI's potential benefits and risks in his address at the Nasdaq. 
 He opened by talking about the technology's potential to advance medicine and cure diseases, and he reiterated the company's pledge to focus on safety and to pace the training and advancement of AI systems.
 "Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so, only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing," Amodei said. "If we can show it's possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same."
 — Ashley Capoot 
 4 Hours Ago Daniela Amodei's message to people who fear AI
 Daniela Amodei, Co-founder and President of Anthropic speaks inside the Nasdaq MarketSite ahead of the anticipated IPO of artificial intelligence company Anthropic in New York City on November 19, 2026. Charly Triballeau | Afp | Getty Images Daniela Amodei spoke from the Nasdaq ahead of the opening bell, and had a message for people who are scared of AI.
 "This technology needs you — not your trust, not your use, but your voice," she said. "The end of this story isn't written yet. Intelligence is now something humans can build. What we choose to build with it is up to all of us."
 —Chris Eudaily 
 5 Hours Ago Retail demand for Anthropic's IPO was largest in history, sources tell CNBC
 watch now VIDEO 8:11 08:11 David Faber, CNBC insiders on what to watch from the Anthropic IPO today Squawk Box Retail demand for Anthropic's IPO was larger than demand for any other deal in history, sources told CNBC's David Faber.
 Anthropic targeted retail allocation of about 20%, as CNBC previously reported, a much higher percentage than the typical initial public offering, which is 5% to 10% for retail investors.
 Anthropic's stock could trade into the low $100s on Thursday, according to the people, who asked not to be named because they were not authorized to speak publicly.
 — Ashley Capoot 
 5 Hours Ago Over 400 Anthropic employees set to be worth $100 million or more
 watch now VIDEO 2:18 02:18 Anthropic's IPO could mint thousands of millionaires — and reshape San Francisco Tech The average Anthropic employee will be worth over $40 million after today's IPO, marking one of the most rapid wealth creation events in history. The AI lab has generated 1.77 billion employee options. Earlier hires stand to benefit even further, with over 400 employees expected to be worth $100 million or more at the current share price. 
 Lockup periods may alter the timeline for the gains to make it to the economy, but the newfound wealth is expected to supercharge the San Francisco real estate market and philanthropic giving.
 — Robert Frank, Caleigh Keating 
 5 Hours Ago Here's what it's like outside the Nasdaq
 Outside the Nasdaq ahead of the Anthropic IPO on Nov. 19th, 2026. Ashley Capoot | CNBC As of around 8:00 a.m. ET, the scene outside the Nasdaq is pretty sleepy, though there is some police presence. The Nasdaq isn't promoting Anthropic's logo yet, but there are some ads for Elon Musk's Grok Bot and the neocloud Nebius .
 — Ashley Capoot 
 5 Hours Ago Amodeis arrive at the Nasdaq

 5 Hours Ago Anthropic IPO to surge 25% when it opens, perpetual futures indicate
 Anthropic PBC signage ahead of the company's initial public offering (IPO) at the Nasdaq MarketSite in New York, US, on Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026. Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Images Anthropic is headed for a big first-day pop, if trading in the perpetual futures market is any indication. The futures in Anthropic on the Hyperliquid exchange were trading above $104, indicating a surge of more than 25% from its $83 IPO price.
 Anthropic trading in so-called perp futures on Polymarket were also showing a jump to similar levels. 
 "Early indications are that it's up about 25%," said J.J. Kinahan, senior VP of retail and alternative investments at CBOE Global Markets, on CNBC "Squawk Box." "With some of the tumultuous times here for Nvidia, a little bit of that trust has gone away from the retail investor so this is the way people I think are going to express themselves."
 Perpetual futures are a crypto-based new type of futures contract which never expire and don't represent any ownership in the companies its tracking. The derivatives correctly predicted the initial pop in the SpaceX IPO back in June. 
 Retail investors are clamoring to buy Anthropic in the open market, according to Vanda Research. Retail net buying will be about $250 million, double that of SpaceX buying, the firm estimates.
 — John Melloy

 7 Hours Ago Academics and industry experts circulate ‘The MisAnthropic Statement’ ahead of listing
 More than 90 academics and AI safety experts signed " The MisAnthropic Statement " ahead of the company's Nasdaq debut, blasting it for amassing power and rushing to build potentially dangerous technology.
 "Anthropic warns that recursively self-improving AI could concentrate power and escape human control, yet races to build it first," the statement says. "The company uses safety branding to court investors, employees, and the public — even as it has quietly weakened its safety pledges and lobbied for self-serving regulation. Anthropic is not a safe AI company, and we must reject its reckless attempt to amass power in the name of the greater good."
 A representative for Anthropic declined to comment about the statement.
 — Ashley Capoot 
 8 Hours Ago Anthropic’s explosive revenue growth 
 The Anthropic Claude logo on a smartphone and laptop arranged in San Francisco, California, Nov. 10, 2026. David Paul Morris | Bloomberg | Getty Images Anthropic's revenue has surged dramatically this year as more companies have adopted its AI models and products. 
 The company said it generated roughly $33.24 billion in revenue for the nine months ended Sept. 30, up roughly 1,200% from the same period last year. 
 Anthropic's losses also widened, however. It reported a $104 billion net loss during the period, compared to a net loss of $25.1 billion over the same stretch in 2025. The vast majority of its loss, about $94.3 billion, comes from a change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities and SAFEs, Anthropic said.
 The company said its run-rate revenue was roughly $81 billion as of the end of October, up roughly $10 billion from the previous month.
 — Ashley Capoot 
 8 Hours Ago Anthropic’s seven co-founders have majority voting power 
 Zoom In Icon Arrows pointing outwards The founders of Anthropic. CNBC Anthropic said in its prospectus that it believes its seven co-founders are "distinctly equipped to be stewards of our mission." 
 The co-founders are the sole members of " Founder LLC ," a new entity that holds 50.1% of the voting power of the company's outstanding shares. The structure gives them "the ability to determine the outcome of all matters submitted to a vote of our stockholders generally for the foreseeable future," according to the filing.
 The co-founders' combined voting power from their holdings and their interest in Founder LLC is expected to be 61.3%, according to the filing.
